summary.headline: GMM Pfaudler Q2 FY27 order intake hit a record INR 1,198 crore (+36% YoY), while reported EBITDA margin was 10.3% due to European loss-makers.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR 1,065 crore and reported EBITDA was INR 110 crore, up 18% QoQ. Reported margin of 10.3% was pulled down by European loss-making entities, which carried an H1 EBITDA loss of about INR 43 crore; excluding them, Q2 margin was 15.9%. Management is executing a European restructuring (UK facility closed, German workforce reduced, Swiss restructuring under way, manufacturing shifting to Poland) and reiterated FY27 guidance. Order backlog reached a record INR 2,446 crore, up 14% YoY. Management deferred granular FY28 margin numbers to an investor day expected in coming months.

segments.name: Corrosion Resistant Technologies (CRT)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 500 crore, flat YoY and +7% QoQ; Q2 order intake INR 556 crore (+15% YoY). H1 revenue INR 966 crore (+5% YoY), H1 orders INR 1,058 crore (+19% YoY).

segments.name: PPT
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 331 crore (+34% YoY, +30% QoQ); Q2 orders INR 364 crore (+85% YoY, flat QoQ). H1 revenue INR 586 crore (+29% YoY), H1 orders INR 731 crore (+74% YoY).

segments.name: HET (Heavy Engineering)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 92 crore (+38% YoY, +24% QoQ); Q2 orders INR 201 crore (+254% YoY). H1 revenue INR 165 crore (+17% YoY), H1 orders INR 258 crore (+306% YoY). Booked out until Q2 next year per management.

segments.name: PST
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 142 crore (+57% YoY, +8% QoQ). H1 revenue INR 273 crore (+51% YoY); H1 orders INR 157 crore, including INR 77 crore in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double-digit.
FY27 reported EBITDA margin guided at about 10%-11%, including loss-making entities.
Adjusted EBITDA margin for the core business guided at 14%-15%; management said about 80% of business operates in that range.
Tax rate target of 30% or lower; FY26 ETR was about 49%. Management expects improvement quarter on quarter and a return to the ballpark target by FY28.
European cost savings expected to show in H2 FY27, with fuller benefit in Q1 FY28 and FY28. Management expects no major additional restructuring cost.
Management expects quarter-on-quarter sequential margin improvement; FY28 is framed as the year transformation benefits show up. FY28 margin numbers deferred to an investor day in coming months.
capex_capacity: Poland facility expansion underway; expected to contribute extra capacity from end FY27 / start FY28.
India factory described as full; heavy engineering booked out until Q2 FY28.
New US facility opened for Edlon to serve existing and future demand.
China glass-lined factory now at full utilisation on CDMO-driven orders.
Germany expected to be at least break-even in H2 FY27 and positive in FY28, per management.
Bulgaria acid recovery (defence) order of about USD 30 million won; further European acid-concentration plant opportunities in discussion.
demand_pricing: Q2 order intake was a record INR 1,198 crore; India orders were a record INR 483 crore, more than double QoQ, driven by large heavy-engineering orders. Non-traditional industries made up 44% of Q2 orders.
Pharma (CDMO and peptides) is the main demand driver for CRT and PPT. Peptide orders from Indian customers were about INR 150 crore over roughly six months.
Chemical demand remains subdued; management is not building in a major chemicals revival.
Glass-lined pricing is improving in India, and management expects better margins from the current backlog as it converts.
Defence (NATO-sponsored TNT and nitrocellulose acid-recovery projects), nuclear (NPCIL, Megha Engineering, planned reactors) and thermal power (LP and HP heaters) are cited as growth areas.
Italy glass-lined order of about USD 5 million won; Middle East and Africa exports in HET are adding to backlog.

qa_highlights.question: What are the European restructuring cost savings targets, margin targets, and restructuring costs, and will they fall in FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the UK closure is complete and Germany's 40+ role reduction was costed last year, with benefits starting in H2 FY27 and fuller in FY28. Swiss restructuring is under way (Swiss entity has about 30 people) with some benefit next year. No large additional restructuring cost is expected; the CEO International role was removed and top-management reorganisation saves cost.

qa_highlights.question: Are gross margins in the backlog better than the P&L shows?
qa_highlights.answer: The backlog was booked in a softer market, but management said Indian glass-lined pricing is improving and operating leverage should lift margins. The CFO expects gross margins to return to historical levels as European losses are reduced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline for the backlog and margins on new orders? Are there more peptide, defence, and emerging-theme orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Backlog is improving across all divisions and geographies. Peptides alone brought about INR 150 crore in Indian orders in six months. Defence is active in Europe (NATO-sponsored TNT and nitrocellulose plants), and semiconductors (Edlon), critical minerals and data centre themes were cited. No specific margin or execution-timeline figures were given for new orders.

qa_highlights.question: Can Poland capacity and the restructuring move margins higher from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Gregory Gelhaus said Poland is being expanded, with capacity arriving around end FY27 and start FY28, and activity is moving there in a phased way due to customer commitments. The CFO said margins should rise sequentially each quarter, with savings in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CRT outlook, given flat YoY revenue, and are chemical capex cycles returning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said chemicals remain subdued with only spot demand in specialty and agrochemicals. Global CRT growth is led by pharma and CDMO in the US, South America, China and India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stable tax rate for FY27 and FY28, and how much will finance costs fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a tax rate of 30% or lower, improving quarter on quarter. It expects lower interest costs than last year, but gave no quantified reduction; forex impact affected the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What trajectory should be expected for EBITDA-to-PAT conversion in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 ETR was about 49%, and moving to 30% or lower, along with removing notional intercompany-loan losses, would lift PAT. Management did not give a year-by-year trajectory and pointed to the investor day.

qa_highlights.question: Can aggregate margin reach 12.5%-13% next year, and what is the exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a FY28 number and asked analysts to wait for the investor day. It said a 15% core EBITDA margin is achievable, India is at 13%-14%, and the company aims to beat its promises.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the peptides and Edlon opportunity, and is M&A planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarak Patel described peptides as a long-term structural opportunity with India able to add capacity faster than Europe. Edlon has a new head with 26 years of experience and a new US facility. No acquisition is planned currently; any deal must bring growth and high profitability.

risks_watch: Reported EBITDA margin (10.3% in Q2) is well below the core 15.9%; the gap depends on the European restructuring delivering savings in H2 FY27 and FY28.
Cost savings and FY28 margin targets have not been quantified; the investor day is expected in coming months.
Tax rate remains about 30%-plus versus a 49% FY26 ETR, and notional intercompany-loan losses continue; refinancing timing and finance-cost benefit are not quantified.
Chemical end-market demand remains weak, so CRT revenue was flat YoY in Q2.
Gross margin fell in Q2 as loss-making entities weighed on it; Q2 PAT of INR 35 crore was below the INR 38 crore of Q2 FY26.
Poland capacity arrives only around end FY27/start FY28, and customer commitments may slow the transfer of manufacturing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order momentum and the core business, but cautious and somewhat evasive on quantified restructuring savings and FY28 margins, repeatedly deferring detail to an investor day in coming months.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 38 crore in Q2 FY26; +59% QoQ

key_quotes: We recorded the highest-ever quarterly order inflow in the company's history, crossing INR1,000 crores for the consecutive quarters and reaching INR1,200 crores with strong India order intake of about INR 483 crores, also being the highest ever and more than double sequentially.
We do not see any major restructuring costs attached with this new restructuring program.
Instead of giving you a number that is, I would say wait a couple of months. The investor day is happening.
But just to clarify here, it is not far off to say as a company, a 15% core business EBITDA margin is not something that is crazy. This is definitely achievable.
I would like to buy a peptide company, but no.
There's no plan right now. There's a lot of work to happen, but at the same time, we keep seeing, meeting, talking, so that's an ongoing process.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at double-digit growth, backed by a record INR 2,446 crore backlog (+14% YoY) and Q2 order intake of INR 1,198 crore (+36% YoY), with Poland expansion due end FY27/start FY28 and European cost savings from H2 FY27; numeric capacity and margin detail is only partial.

rows.label: Germany at least break-even, positive in FY28
